title: Biblical Hospitality in the Church
definition: Biblical Hospitality in the Church is the welcoming, generous, and Christlike care shown to believers, strangers, and those in need.
summary: Biblical Hospitality in the Church is the welcoming of believers and strangers into fellowship, care, and shared life.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomed sinners and teaches His people to receive others with grace and truth.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on hospitality as a congregational practice of welcome. It includes meals, homes, conversations, space at the table, and intentional inclusion of those who might remain unseen. Hospitality in the church turns fellowship from a slogan into embodied love.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people can attend church and still feel unknown. Hospitality fights cliques, loneliness, and partiality by making room for others. It gives practical expression to the Gospel welcome believers have received from Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Invite people in before they have to prove they belong socially. Notice newcomers, singles, the disabled, the grieving, and those without natural connections. Use your home, table, time, and attention as instruments of grace.
